sources.ref_file_title: CHKV25 - Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption from Linear Homomorphism and Sparse LPN
sources.authors: Henry Corrigan-Gibbs, Alexandra Henzinger, Yael Tauman Kalai, Vinod Vaikuntanathan
sources.note: Abstract explicitly offers DDH as an instantiating assumption for the linearly homomorphic component.

pages.class_justification: CHKV25 make no RTV-style claim. The construction uses the linearly homomorphic PKE generically, but the sparse-LPN component is a concrete algebraic scheme; recording a class the source does not state would add a claim.
pages.statement: [[learning-parity-with-noise#sparse-learning-parity-with-noise|Sparse LPN]] together with any linearly homomorphic public-key encryption yields [[homomorphic-encryption#somewhat-homomorphic-encryption-she|somewhat homomorphic encryption]]; instantiating the linearly homomorphic scheme under [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]] gives SHE from DDH and sparse LPN. The scheme evaluates $O(\log \secpar / \log \log \secpar)$ homomorphic multiplications followed by $\poly(\secpar)$ additions, with ciphertext length a fixed polynomial in $\secpar$ independent of the supported number of operations — [[CHKV25 - Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption from Linear Homomorphism and Sparse LPN|CHKV25]].
flags: OVER-SPLIT (migration note is correct): this edge is the DDH instantiation of the generic theorem recorded on partially-homomorphic-encryption-phe-and-sparse-learning-parity-with-noise-to-somewhat-homomorphic-encryption-she-chkv25 composed with DDH => linearly homomorphic PKE. CHKV25's abstract does state the DDH instantiation explicitly, so the edge is citable as-is, but the verifier should decide whether the wiki keeps both the generic edge and its DDH/DCR instantiations.
The genuinely-conjunctive structure (both hypotheses needed) is correct as recorded.

sources.ref_file_title: DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications
sources.authors: Nico Döttling, Sanjam Garg, Yuval Ishai, Giulio Malavolta, Tamer Mour, Rafail Ostrovsky
sources.note: Abstract: TDH with one-bit hints from DDH, QR, DCR, or LWE; polylog-communication PIR from DDH or QR.

pages.class_justification: DGI+19 do not classify the reduction; the construction is a concrete group-based scheme from an assumption, so the RTV primitive-from-primitive taxonomy is not stated by the source.
pages.model_justification: The DDH-based construction is in the standard model (no idealized oracle).
pages.statement: [[DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications|DGI+19]] construct [[trapdoor-hash-function|trapdoor hash functions]] for the class of index predicates $f_i(x) = x_i$, with hints of a single bit, from [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]]; the framework also admits instantiations from QR, DCR, and LWE. The DDH-based TDH yields two-message single-server PIR with $\polylog(n)$ communication — [[DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications|DGI+19]].
pages.sketch: The hash key is a $2 \times n$ matrix of group elements and the hash of $x \in \bits^n$ is the subset product $\prod_j g_{j, x_j}$. An encoding key for index $i$ is the entrywise $s$-th power of the hash key with the $i$-th column additionally perturbed by an extra generator, so evaluating on $x$ yields the hashed value's $s$-th power shifted by $x_i$; the trapdoor $s$ recovers $x_i$ from the hash, and DDH hides which column is perturbed, hence the index $i$.
notes_to_keep: DGI+19's DDH-based TDH has its own rate/parameter constraints (one-bit hints, rate-1 variants) that the edge cannot carry; they are load-bearing for the downstream polylog-communication PIR claim.
flags: COMPOSITE chain correctly split by migration: DDH => TDH (this page) and TDH => PIR (separate pages, e.g. tdh-to-cpir-amr25) are separate links, both in DGI+19.

pages.class_justification: The construction side is the identity (the LWE instance is unchanged) and the reduction is one fixed algorithm that runs any search-LWE solver once as an oracle and post-processes its output with a residual check. This is the RTV04 fully-black-box shape, degenerately instantiated for an assumption-to-assumption edge.
pages.statement: If [[learning-with-errors#decision-lwe|Decision LWE]] is hard for $(n, q, \chi, m)$ then [[learning-with-errors#search-lwe|Search LWE]] is hard for the same parameters: any efficient algorithm recovering $\mathbf{s}$ from LWE samples yields a decision distinguisher with essentially the same advantage — folklore.
pages.sketch: Given a challenge $(\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{u})$, run the search solver to obtain a candidate $\hat{\mathbf{s}}$ and accept iff $\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{A}\hat{\mathbf{s}}$ is a plausible error vector. On LWE samples the check passes whenever the solver succeeds; on uniform samples, for $m$ sufficiently larger than $n$, no candidate secret leaves a small residual except with negligible probability.
flags: HIGH PRIORITY - SWAPPED BODIES: the migrated quote on this page describes the coordinate-by-coordinate reduction that uses a DECISION oracle to solve SEARCH. Under the repo's hardness-implication convention that reduction proves search-hard => decision-hard, i.e. it belongs on the converse page search-lwe-to-decision-lwe (batch red-29), whose own migrated quote (solve-and-check) in turn belongs here. The two pages' Statement quotes must be exchanged; coordinate with red-29.

The displaced coordinate-recovery reduction is due to Reg05 and requires q = poly(n) (prime q); its O(q n m) sample count and the modulus restriction should travel with it to search-lwe-to-decision-lwe, which should become disposition sourced (Reg05) rather than folklore.

The solve-and-check distinguisher needs the error distribution to be efficiently recognizable (e.g. bounded or discrete Gaussian with a tail cut) and m large enough that a uniform u is far from every A*s; standard for the parameters on the LWE page.

pages.wrong_reason: Misattribution, as the page's own SUSPECT note already says. KSW08's inner-product predicate encryption scheme is NOT proven secure under DLIN: the construction lives in a composite-order bilinear group whose order N is a product of three primes, and its attribute-hiding proof rests on two new subgroup-decision-flavoured assumptions that KSW08 justify only in the generic group model (verified against the paper: it introduces the two new assumptions and proves them generically; DLIN appears nowhere as the hypothesis). The claim 'DLIN implies attribute-hiding IPPE' is true but belongs to a different paper: the first adaptively secure, fully attribute-hiding inner-product encryption under DLIN is Okamoto-Takashima, 'Adaptively Attribute-Hiding (Hierarchical) Inner Product Encryption', EUROCRYPT 2012 (eprint 2011/543). Correct repair: either re-source this edge as KSW08's actual theorem (composite-order subgroup-decision assumptions => IPPE) or retitle it dlin-to-ippe-ot12 with OT12 as source; the source bullet on inner-product-predicate-encryption.md should be fixed in the same pass.
flags: The migration's SUSPECT note is confirmed correct: KSW08 uses two new assumptions in composite-order (N = pqr) bilinear groups, proven only in the generic group model, not DLIN.

If the KSW08 variant of this edge is kept, its hypotheses have no wiki page (the two KSW08 assumptions are nonstandard and unnamed); the OT12 variant would let the existing decisional-linear hypothesis stand.

pages.class_justification: Identity construction: the cPIR protocol runs the DEPIR algorithms unchanged (the server runs Setup on its own database, the client runs Qry/Fin), and any cPIR privacy adversary is verbatim a DEPIR privacy adversary. Both the construction and the reduction use their objects only as oracles. This justification is scoped to the unkeyed (default) variant; see flags.
pages.statement: A [[doubly-efficient-pir|DEPIR]] scheme is by definition a [[single-server-private-information-retrieval|single-server PIR]] whose database is preprocessed before queries: in the unkeyed (default) setting the server runs $\Setup(1^\secpar, DB)$ itself and the query phase is an ordinary two-message single-server PIR with query-time communication and computation $o(n)$; correctness and query privacy carry over unchanged — folklore.
notes_to_keep: Definitional specialization ('is a type of'), not a theorem with a proof in some paper; the folklore label is the citation.
flags: SCOPE CAVEAT: the implication is definitional only for the unkeyed variant (and for PK-DEPIR if the honestly generated key is published, since PK-DEPIR privacy holds even given k). For SK-DEPIR it fails: privacy holds only against adversaries not given k, so a server that runs Setup itself gets no guarantee, and a client cannot preprocess a database it does not hold. Consider narrowing the hypothesis to [[doubly-efficient-pir#unkeyed-depir|unkeyed DEPIR]] or stating the caveat on the page.
The migration note 'implication direction is DEPIR => single-server PIR, opposite to the surface word order' is resolved: the recorded orientation (hypotheses: depir, conclusion: cpir) is correct.

sources.authors: Elette Boyle, Kai-Min Chung, Rafael Pass
sources.note: Shows iO implies diO for pairs of circuits differing on at most polynomially many inputs; also the standard citable statement of the trivial diO => iO direction.

sources.ref_file_title: GGHW14 - On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input
sources.authors: Sanjam Garg, Craig Gentry, Shai Halevi, Daniel Wichs
sources.note: Evidence that general diO with arbitrary auxiliary input does not exist, so the blanket equivalence with iO is implausible.

pages.class_justification: Identity construction: the diO obfuscator is used unchanged as the iO obfuscator. The reduction is fixed: an iO distinguisher for a functionally equivalent pair is directly a diO adversary for the constant sampler outputting that pair, which is unconditionally differing-inputs-hard because no differing input exists.
pages.statement: A [[indistinguishability-obfuscation#differing-inputs-obfuscation-dio|differing-inputs obfuscator]] for a circuit class is an [[indistinguishability-obfuscation|indistinguishability obfuscator]] for the same class: functionally equivalent circuits admit no differing input, so every pair of equivalent circuits is a trivially differing-inputs-hard sampler and the diO guarantee applies — folklore.
pages.improvements_text:
- [[indistinguishability-obfuscation|iO]] for a class implies diO for pairs of circuits in the class that differ on at most polynomially many inputs — [[BCP14 - On Extractability Obfuscation|BCP14]]
- General-purpose diO with arbitrary auxiliary input is implausible: assuming special-purpose obfuscation, there are differing-inputs-hard samplers whose obfuscations are efficiently distinguishable — [[GGHW14 - On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input|GGHW14]]
flags: HIGH PRIORITY - KIND: the recorded kind: equivalence is unsupported. Blanket diO <=> iO is neither proven nor believed: the converse (iO => diO) is known only for circuits differing on at most polynomially many inputs (BCP14), and general diO with auxiliary input is implausible (GGHW14). Set kind to implication (diO => iO, matching the frontmatter orientation); the vague migrated sentence 'equivalent under certain conditions' refers to the BCP14 restricted case, now recorded in improvements.

The trivial direction assumes the standard diO definition quantifying over all (non-uniform) differing-inputs samplers (as in ABGSZ13/BCP14), so constant samplers outputting an equivalent pair are admissible.
If an io-to-dio page restricted to polynomially many differing inputs is ever wanted, it is a separate BCP14-sourced edge, not this one.

pages.wrong_reason: Not a well-defined edge, as the page's own migration notes already concede. The hypotheses pair a protocol (distributed key generation) with generic homomorphic encryption, and no theorem anywhere states that generic HE plus a DKG yields threshold PKE: threshold decryption requires scheme-specific key-sharing and partial-decryption structure that generic (even linear) homomorphism does not provide, and both hypothesis identifiers were invented during migration (neither has a wiki page). The migrated sentence is a parenthetical construction sketch of threshold Paillier on the DCR page; the attributable result is DCR => threshold PKE via threshold Paillier, due to Fouque-Poupard-Stern ('Sharing Decryption in the Context of Voting or Lotteries', FC 2000) and Damgard-Jurik ('A Generalisation, a Simplification and Some Applications of Paillier's Probabilistic Public-Key System', PKC 2001), with dealer-free distributed key generation for the modulus a further separate line of work. Correct repair: delete this edge and record dcr-to-tpke sourced to FPS00 and/or DJ01, updating the '- standard' label on decisional-composite-residuosity.md in the same pass.
flags: The '- standard' folklore label on the source bullet is misapplied: threshold Paillier is attributable (FPS00, DJ01), matching the migration note.

sources.ref_file_title: FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications
sources.authors: Georg Fuchsbauer, Eike Kiltz, Julian Loss
sources.note: Abstract: tight security reduction for the BLS signature scheme to DLOG in the AGM.

pages.class_justification: An AGM reduction reads the algebraic representations the adversary outputs, so it is not black-box in the RTV sense, and FKL18 make no RTV-style classification; the model axis (algebraic-group) carries the restriction.
pages.model_justification: FKL18's BLS analysis is in the AGM combined with the random-oracle model (BLS hashes messages into the group; H is modeled as a random oracle). The model field can carry one value; algebraic-group is recorded and the ROM component is stated in the statement text.
pages.statement: In the [[algebraic-group-model|algebraic group model]], with the hash-to-group function modeled as a random oracle, EUF-CMA security of [[digital-signature#bls-signatures|BLS signatures]] reduces tightly to [[discrete-logarithm|DLOG]]: any efficient algebraic forger yields a DLOG solver with essentially the same running time and success probability — [[FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications|FKL18]].
pages.sketch: The reduction embeds the DLOG challenge in the BLS public key and programs the random oracle on message queries; an algebraic forger outputs its forgery together with a representation in terms of the generator, the public key, and previously seen hash values and signatures, and a valid forgery then yields an equation over the unknown exponent that the reduction solves.
notes_to_keep: The reduction holds only for algebraic adversaries (AGM) and additionally uses the ROM; in the standard model BLS is proven from CDH in the ROM with a non-tight reduction, not from DLOG.
flags: BROKEN CONCLUSION ID: frontmatter conclusion boneh-lynn-shacham-signature has no page and no alias; BLS signatures live at digital-signature#bls-signatures (which the header prose already links). Repoint the conclusion or create the page.

MODEL: the single-valued model field cannot express AGM+ROM. The repo elsewhere encodes ROM as an explicit hypothesis object (cf. dlog-and-rom-to-schnorr-signatures-sch91); either add rom as a hypothesis or keep model algebraic-group with the ROM stated in the page body, but be consistent across the FKL18 edges.

sources.ref_file_title: FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications
sources.authors: Georg Fuchsbauer, Eike Kiltz, Julian Loss
sources.note: Abstract: CDH (among other assumptions) shown equivalent to DLOG in the AGM.

pages.class_justification: The reduction extracts from the algebraic representation the AGM obliges the adversary to output, so it is not black-box in the RTV sense and FKL18 make no RTV-style classification; the model axis carries the restriction.
pages.model_justification: Load-bearing, as the migration note says: the reduction works only for algebraic adversaries; no standard-model reduction from DLOG hardness to CDH hardness is known.
pages.statement: In the [[algebraic-group-model|algebraic group model]], [[computational-diffie-hellman|CDH]] is as hard as [[discrete-logarithm|DLOG]]: any algebraic CDH adversary converts into a DLOG solver with the same advantage and essentially the same running time, so DLOG hardness implies CDH hardness for algebraic adversaries — [[FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications|FKL18]].
pages.sketch: Given a DLOG instance $W = g^z$ in a prime-order group, the reduction runs the algebraic CDH adversary on $(W g^{r}, W g^{s})$ for known random $r, s$. The adversary returns its answer together with coefficients expressing it as a product of powers of the received elements; a correct answer forces a monic quadratic equation in $z$, whose roots the reduction computes over $\ZZ_p$ and checks against $W$.
pages.security_loss: tight: same advantage and essentially the same running time (FKL18)
notes_to_keep: MODEL IS LOAD-BEARING: the reduction holds only for algebraic adversaries; dropping model: algebraic-group would turn a model-relative reduction into a standard-model implication that is not known.
flags: The page's second migrated quote (composing 'these reductions' with the Sho97 generic-group lower bound to get concrete bounds against 'algebraic-and-generic adversaries') is a separate lower-bound statement, not part of this edge; per the migration REPAIR PATCH note it should move to a barrier/lower-bound record, and its AGM-to-GGM transfer step is contested by KZ22 (cf. barrier no-agm-to-ggm-kz22).

FKL18 state an equivalence (CDH =_AGM DLOG); the converse hardness direction (CDH hard => DLOG hard) is the trivial standard-model edge and exists as the separate page cdh-to-dlog, so kind stays implication on both.

pages.class_justification: Membership of a problem in a complexity class is proved by any argument at all; free is the repo convention for proven complexity containments.
pages.statement: The decision version of [[discrete-logarithm|DLOG]] — given $(\GG, g, p, X, t)$, decide whether the exponent $x \in [p]$ with $g^x = X$ satisfies $x \le t$ — lies in [[co-nondeterministic-polynomial-time|coNP]]: the unique exponent $x$ itself certifies a no-instance, and a certificate for the order of $g$ (its prime factorization with primality certificates) makes uniqueness and the verification polynomial-time checkable — folklore.
notes_to_keep: `class: free` because a containment between complexity classes is proved by any argument at all; the reduction-class axis does not discriminate here.
flags: The migrated quote states DLOG in NP intersect coNP; this page records the coNP half and the companion dlog-to-np (batch red-08) records the NP half — the statements should mirror each other.
Stale boilerplate: the Notes still carry the '`class: unstated`' explanation although the frontmatter already says class: free; drop it.

DLOG is a search/promise problem; the containment is about its natural decision version (threshold on the exponent), which the statement now makes explicit. The certificate needs the group order and generator to be verifiable (Pratt-style primality certificates in concrete groups like Z_p^*); with the wiki's GrGen promise the order p is given.
